# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 66 (Bi-Vb Pc66)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc66
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 66
**Title (English, from literature):** Ordaining an untrained married girl
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Paripuṇṇadvādasavassa-asikkhita-gihigata* is the sixty-sixth rule in the *Pācittiya* section of the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga*. The rule establishes that a nun incurs an offense requiring confession if she ordains a married girl who has completed twelve years of age but has not finished the required two-year training period [Hüsken 1997]. In her study of the Theravāda nun's Vinaya, Ute Hüsken notes that the canonical background narrative details the conferral of the training agreement (*sikkhāsammuti*), which must precede the two-year probationary period as a *sikkhamānā* [Hüsken 1997]. While the canonical rule explicitly requires the married girl to have reached twelve years of age before receiving permission to train in the six rules, the commentary in the *Samantapāsādikā* states that this permission may be granted to a married girl as young as ten, silently smoothing over a canonical discrepancy [Hüsken 1997]. An English translation of the rule and its commentary has been published by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

Direct parallels to this rule are preserved in the Pali *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* (Pc 66) and *Bhikkhunī Parivāra* (Pc 66), as well as in the Chinese translation of the Mahāsāṅghika *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* (Pc 102) and its *Pātimokkha*, and the Sanskrit Lokottaravāda *Bhikṣuṇī Vibhaṅga* (Pc 102).
